# Writing the piece

Before you write, ask the user for what you are missing. Send one message with at most five questions, the most useful first. Ask only what would change the piece and what the request does not already answer. When the answers come back, write the piece as you normally would, and hand it over. When the user does not know something, write without it and do not guess.

Before I draft, a few questions. The answers will change what the letter says.

1. **What is the "a third will close within a year" figure based on?** None of the facts you gave lead to it. Is there a survey of your 38 pharmacies, a pharmacists' association estimate, or something else? If the plan or a reporter can't find a source, they can dismiss that line and the rest of the letter with it. If there's no source, I'd say something you can back up, such as how many of your 38 say they can't keep taking plan members at these rates. Also, how many independent pharmacies are in the state in total?

2. **What exactly do you want the plan to do before July 1?** For example: put a rule in the new PBM contract that pharmacies are paid at least what the drug costs plus a dispensing fee, require the PBM to show its pricing, or meet with you before renewal. The more specific the request, the harder it is to ignore.

3. **Who signs it, and can it name names?** Will all 38 pharmacies be listed with their towns? Are you willing to be named as the contact? And do you want to name the plan and the PBM?

4. **What does this mean in dollars for you?** At $1.80 a fill, your 3,100 plan prescriptions come to about $5,600 a year, but only if they were all among those 20 generics. Do you know your actual yearly loss on plan members, or roughly what share of your plan fills are those 20 drugs? I'll avoid any figure we can't defend.

5. **Is there one real patient or town we can point to?** For instance, a county where the closest other pharmacy is an hour away, or a state employee (anonymous is fine) who would lose their pharmacy. Have you raised this with the plan before, and did they answer?

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write the letter without them.

<final_document>
**An open letter to the [State Employees' Health Plan]**

From the Main Street Pharmacy Alliance, 38 independent pharmacies serving state employees across [State]

Since January, your plan has paid us less to fill your members' most common prescriptions than it costs us to fill them.

We looked at the 20 generic drugs we fill most often. On average, the plan pays us $1.80 less per prescription than we pay to buy the drug and fill it. Members of your plan make up about 22% of the prescriptions at our 38 pharmacies. That means we lose money on one of our biggest groups of customers every day. Some of us make back part of that loss on brand-name drugs. That doesn't change what is happening with the generics your members pick up most often.

This is already affecting where state employees can fill their prescriptions. Two of our 38 pharmacies have told us they will stop filling for plan members if the rates stay the same. Nine independent pharmacies in the state have closed in the past two years. We can't say how many of those closings were caused by payment rates. We can say that every closing leaves fewer places for people to go.

In some parts of the state, there is no other place to go. In 14 counties, the nearest pharmacy for most people is an independent one. The nearest chain pharmacy is more than 20 miles away. If one of those pharmacies stops taking your plan, a teacher, a state trooper or a retired state worker there has to drive that distance to fill a prescription, or go without.

Your contract with your pharmacy benefit manager, the company that sets what pharmacies are paid, comes up for renewal on July 1. That renewal is the chance to fix this. We ask that the new contract pay pharmacies at least what a drug costs us, plus a fee for filling it.

We will help you check our numbers. We will share our purchase invoices for all 20 drugs with your staff. I will meet with them at any time before May 1, so this can be settled well before the contract is signed.

Our pharmacies know your members by name. We want to keep serving them, and we're asking for terms that let us.

Sincerely,

Tom Reilly
Owner, Reilly Drug, Carver
On behalf of the Main Street Pharmacy Alliance
[phone] · [email]
</final_document>

**What I changed or left out:**
- **The "a third will close" claim is gone.** In its place the letter says two of your 38 pharmacies will stop filling for plan members, which you can back up. I didn't name those two.
- **The nine closings aren't blamed on rates.** The letter says outright that you can't show how many closed because of rates. That keeps the plan or a reporter from using that line to discredit you.
- **I didn't estimate your own loss.** You don't know what share of your 3,100 plan fills are those 20 drugs, so I couldn't calculate it. I also left the 3,100 figure out to keep the letter to one page. If you want a personal line, you could add: "Last year my pharmacy filled about 3,100 prescriptions for plan members."
- **The brand-name offset is mentioned on purpose.** The plan will probably raise it, and saying it first makes you look straightforward instead of caught out.

**My recommendations on your open questions:**
- **Name the plan, not the PBM.** The plan decides on the renewal, so the letter should be aimed at them. Naming the PBM doesn't help your request and makes the dispute bigger.
- **List all 38 pharmacies and their towns below the signature, if all 38 agree.** Seeing pharmacies from their own region is what makes newspaper readers and legislators pay attention. A full list doesn't single out the two that may stop taking the plan. If some won't sign, leave the list off and keep "38 independent pharmacies" in the heading.

**Still to fill in:**
- The plan's official name, the state, and your contact details.
- The fill fee: the letter doesn't give an amount. If the alliance agrees on a number, adding it makes the request stronger.
- Dates: July 1 and May 1 have no year. Add 2027 if that's the renewal you mean.
- Before you publish, find out whether anyone in the alliance has already raised this with the plan. If they have, mention it.
